question: Do two fully independent capture processes of the same build agree, state for state, on both the media and the rendered frame?
distinctStatesNote: rest and pointer-center coincide by construction; both are named in the required state list and both are captured, but they count once.
mismatchIsPositional: One state differs per run and it is a different state each time (partial-viewport on one pair, pointer-right on the next). This is residual per-run nondeterminism, not a specific broken state.
whatHadToBeFixedToGetHere: setTime() never paused the clips, so a capture pinned nothing at all.
Reading the media state after resume() measured the resume, not the freeze.
A fixed settle delay left pointer and rotation mid-ease; the capture now polls the motion state until it stops changing.
Freezing before positioning the grid pinned whichever clips happened to be decoded at that moment; positioning now happens first.

A fresh browser context per state made every state decode its clips independently, and two states with byte-identical specs produced different frames. States sharing a viewport now share one warmed-up page, which is what made rest and pointer-center agree.
The scan picked each content extreme independently, which collapsed high-texture onto bright and voided the mandatory-high-texture safeguard. The scan now forces four distinct cells.

readMediaState() returned frameWait:'presented' and seekError:0 as constants, which made a caller believe a decoded frame had been verified when nothing had been. It now returns only what it can actually read.
The frozen gate briefly required the decoder to land on round(mediaTime*30); the clips are not all 30 fps, so that rejected good captures. It is reported, not gated.
residualWeakness: One state per run still differs between processes. The count still meets the >=12 requirement, but which state drops is not predictable, so a key state could be the one blocked in a given round.

sourceIntegrity.method: glass-lab-v4 draws a checker scene with no video. reset() and pause() predate Stage H, so the same pin works on either build; without the pin two runs of one build already differ.
